amendments.decisions: WP 8 stage 3a: regionChest relabelled Chest region (IC-809); id and hierarchy unchanged

description: Proposed anatomy hierarchy (OQ-22). L1 region, L2 muscle group, L3 anatomical muscle or named functional muscle set whose members cannot be trained separately, L4 head, part or named member of such a set. sort orders siblings (ascending, step 10). lifecycle is active or retired (retired nodes stay in the file and in ledger.json; ids are never reused). Qualitative only; no activation values.

nodes.label: Neck
nodes.definition: The cervical region between the skull and the upper trunk.
nodes.includes: Muscles whose main job is to flex, extend, tilt or rotate the head and neck.
nodes.excludes: Upper trapezius and levator scapulae (tagged under Upper back as scapular muscles).

nodes.label: Neck flexors
nodes.definition: Muscles at the front of the neck that bend the head and neck forward.
nodes.includes: Sternocleidomastoid and deep neck flexors.
nodes.excludes: Muscles that lift the head backwards.

nodes.label: Sternocleidomastoid
nodes.definition: Paired muscle running from behind the ear to the breastbone and collarbone.
nodes.includes: Neck flexion (both sides), side flexion and rotation to the opposite side (one side).
nodes.note: Also a lateral flexor and rotator; filed once under flexors.

nodes.label: Deep neck flexors
nodes.definition: Longus colli and longus capitis, the deep muscles on the front of the cervical spine.
nodes.includes: Chin-tuck movements and controlled neck flexion.

nodes.label: Neck extensors
nodes.definition: Muscles at the back of the neck that tilt the head back and hold it upright.
nodes.includes: Splenius, semispinalis capitis and suboccipitals.

nodes.label: Splenius capitis and cervicis
nodes.definition: Strap muscles on the back of the neck.
nodes.includes: Neck extension and rotation to the same side.

nodes.label: Semispinalis capitis
nodes.definition: Thick column of muscle beside the cervical spine.
nodes.includes: Neck extension.

nodes.label: Suboccipital muscles
nodes.definition: Small muscles at the base of the skull.
nodes.includes: Fine head positioning and upper cervical extension.
nodes.note: Rarely a training target; kept so mobility entries can be tagged.

nodes.label: Neck side flexors
nodes.definition: Muscles that tilt the head sideways.
nodes.includes: Scalenes.
nodes.excludes: Sternocleidomastoid, which is filed under flexors.

nodes.label: Scalenes
nodes.definition: Anterior, middle and posterior scalene muscles on the side of the neck.
nodes.includes: Neck side flexion and elevation of the first and second ribs.

nodes.label: Shoulder
nodes.definition: The shoulder joint and the muscles that move or stabilise the arm at the shoulder.
nodes.includes: Deltoid and rotator cuff.
nodes.excludes: Muscles that mainly move the shoulder blade (see Chest and Back) and the chest muscles that cross the shoulder.

nodes.label: Shoulders
nodes.definition: Muscle group of the deltoid, the main mover of the arm at the shoulder.
nodes.includes: The deltoid and its three heads.
nodes.excludes: Rotator cuff (own group) and scapular muscles.

nodes.label: Deltoid
nodes.definition: The rounded shoulder muscle with front, side and rear fibres.
nodes.includes: Shoulder flexion, abduction, extension and horizontal movement of the arm.

nodes.label: Front delts
nodes.definition: Anterior head of the deltoid.
nodes.includes: Shoulder flexion and pressing overhead; assists in horizontal adduction.
nodes.excludes: Chest muscles that dominate flat pressing.
nodes.note: Anterior deltoid. Preserved WP 8 id (L4 head).

nodes.label: Side delts
nodes.definition: Lateral head of the deltoid.
nodes.includes: Shoulder abduction (raising the arm out to the side).
nodes.excludes: Supraspinatus, which helps start abduction but sits in the rotator cuff.
nodes.note: Lateral deltoid. Preserved WP 8 id (L4 head).

nodes.label: Rear delts
nodes.definition: Posterior head of the deltoid.
nodes.includes: Shoulder extension and horizontal abduction (reverse fly).
nodes.excludes: Rhomboids and middle trapezius, which retract the shoulder blade.
nodes.note: Posterior deltoid. Preserved WP 8 id (L4 head).

nodes.label: Rotator cuff
nodes.definition: Four small muscles that centre the head of the humerus in the shoulder socket.
nodes.includes: Supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor, subscapularis.

nodes.label: Supraspinatus
nodes.definition: Cuff muscle in the hollow above the spine of the shoulder blade.
nodes.includes: Helping to start shoulder abduction and centring the humerus; it works with the deltoid through the whole arc.

nodes.label: Infraspinatus
nodes.definition: Cuff muscle below the shoulder blade spine.
nodes.includes: Shoulder external rotation.

nodes.label: Teres minor
nodes.definition: Small cuff muscle on the upper part of the lateral (outer) border of the shoulder blade.
nodes.includes: Shoulder external rotation.

nodes.label: Subscapularis
nodes.definition: Cuff muscle on the front of the shoulder blade.
nodes.includes: Shoulder internal rotation.

nodes.label: Chest region
nodes.definition: The front of the ribcage and the muscles that lie over it.
nodes.includes: Pectoral muscles and serratus anterior.
nodes.excludes: Deltoid, which is a shoulder muscle.

nodes.label: Chest
nodes.definition: Muscle group covering the pectorals and serratus anterior.
nodes.includes: Pressing and fly movements that load the pectorals.
nodes.note: Preserved WP 8 id (L2 group).

nodes.label: Pectoralis major
nodes.definition: Large fan-shaped muscle of the upper chest wall.
nodes.includes: Horizontal adduction, shoulder flexion and internal rotation, pressing.

nodes.label: Pectoralis major, clavicular head
nodes.definition: Upper fibres attaching to the collarbone.
nodes.includes: Incline pressing and shoulder flexion at the chest.
nodes.note: Qualitative emphasis only; incline angles shift emphasis, they do not isolate it.

nodes.label: Pectoralis major, sternocostal head
nodes.definition: Middle and lower fibres attaching to the breastbone and ribs.
nodes.includes: Flat and decline pressing, dips and fly movements. Includes the abdominal fibres.
nodes.note: Abdominal fibres are not tagged separately.

nodes.label: Pectoralis minor
nodes.definition: Small muscle under pectoralis major, attaching to the shoulder blade.
nodes.includes: Shoulder blade protraction and depression.
nodes.note: Scapular function; placed under Chest as planned.

nodes.label: Serratus anterior
nodes.definition: Muscle along the side of the ribcage attaching to the shoulder blade.
nodes.includes: Shoulder blade protraction and upward rotation (push-up plus, overhead reach).
nodes.note: Scapular function; placed under Chest as planned.

nodes.label: Back
nodes.definition: The posterior trunk from the base of the neck to the pelvis.
nodes.includes: Muscles of the upper back, the lats and the lower back.

nodes.label: Upper back
nodes.definition: Muscles between the neck and the mid-spine that move and stabilise the shoulder blades.
nodes.includes: Trapezius, rhomboids and levator scapulae.
nodes.excludes: Lats, rear delts and spinal extensors.
nodes.note: Preserved WP 8 id (L2 group). Label in training taxonomy: Upper back (traps, rhomboids).

nodes.label: Trapezius
nodes.definition: Kite-shaped muscle from the skull base and neck down to the 12th thoracic vertebra (T12), working in three parts.
nodes.includes: Shoulder blade elevation, retraction, depression and upward rotation.

nodes.label: Upper trapezius
nodes.definition: Upper fibres running from neck to collarbone.
nodes.includes: Shrugging and shoulder blade elevation.
nodes.note: Also extends and side-flexes the neck.

nodes.label: Middle trapezius
nodes.definition: Horizontal fibres between spine and shoulder blade.
nodes.includes: Shoulder blade retraction.

nodes.label: Lower trapezius
nodes.definition: Lower fibres running down the spine as far as the 12th thoracic vertebra (T12).
nodes.includes: Shoulder blade depression and upward rotation.

nodes.label: Rhomboids
nodes.definition: Rhomboid major and minor beneath the trapezius.
nodes.includes: Shoulder blade retraction and downward rotation.
nodes.note: Major and minor are not tagged separately.

nodes.label: Levator scapulae
nodes.definition: Muscle from the upper neck vertebrae to the shoulder blade.
nodes.includes: Shoulder blade elevation.
nodes.note: Debatable: also a neck muscle; filed as a scapular muscle.

nodes.label: Lats
nodes.definition: Muscle group of the latissimus dorsi and teres major.
nodes.includes: Pulling the arm down and back, and pulling the body up.
nodes.note: Preserved WP 8 id (L2 group).

nodes.label: Latissimus dorsi
nodes.definition: Broad muscle from the spine and pelvis to the upper arm.
nodes.includes: Shoulder extension, adduction and internal rotation; vertical and horizontal pulling.

nodes.label: Teres major
nodes.definition: Thick muscle below the shoulder blade that assists the lats.
nodes.includes: Shoulder extension, adduction and internal rotation.
nodes.note: Functionally a shoulder muscle; filed under Lats as planned.

nodes.label: Lower back
nodes.definition: Muscles that extend and stabilise the lumbar spine.
nodes.includes: Erector spinae, quadratus lumborum and multifidus.
nodes.note: Preserved WP 8 id (L2 group).

nodes.label: Erector spinae
nodes.definition: Group of muscle columns running along the spine (iliocostalis, longissimus and spinalis).
nodes.includes: Spinal extension and isometric bracing in hinges and carries. The three columns are not modelled separately.
nodes.note: Thoracic portions also serve the upper back; tag here. No L4 split: the three columns cannot be loaded separately.

nodes.label: Quadratus lumborum
nodes.definition: Deep muscle linking the pelvis to the lowest rib.
nodes.includes: Side flexion of the trunk and anti-lateral-flexion bracing.
nodes.note: Debatable: sits deep in the abdominal wall; filed under Lower back as planned.

nodes.label: Multifidus
nodes.definition: Short deep muscles along the vertebrae.
nodes.includes: Fine control and stiffening of the spine.

nodes.label: Arm
nodes.definition: The upper arm and forearm.
nodes.includes: Elbow flexors and extensors and the muscles that move the forearm, wrist and fingers.

nodes.label: Upper arm, front
nodes.definition: Muscles at the front of the upper arm that bend the elbow.
nodes.includes: Biceps, brachialis, coracobrachialis.

nodes.label: Biceps
nodes.definition: Biceps brachii with two heads.
nodes.includes: Elbow flexion, forearm supination and shoulder flexion.
nodes.note: Preserved WP 8 id (L3 muscle).

nodes.label: Biceps, long head
nodes.definition: Outer head crossing the top of the shoulder joint.
nodes.includes: Curls with the arm behind or beside the body.
nodes.note: Emphasis claims are qualitative. L4 tag; use only when the design deliberately shifts the load.

nodes.label: Biceps, short head
nodes.definition: Inner head, attached to the coracoid process of the shoulder blade.
nodes.includes: Curls with the arm in front of the body.
nodes.note: Emphasis claims are qualitative. L4 tag; use only when the design deliberately shifts the load.

nodes.label: Brachialis
nodes.definition: Muscle under the biceps that bends the elbow in any forearm position.
nodes.includes: Hammer and reverse curls.

nodes.label: Coracobrachialis
nodes.definition: Small muscle at the top of the inner upper arm.
nodes.includes: Shoulder flexion and adduction.
nodes.note: Rarely a training target.

nodes.label: Upper arm, back
nodes.definition: Muscles at the back of the upper arm that straighten the elbow.
nodes.includes: Triceps and anconeus.

nodes.label: Triceps
nodes.definition: Triceps brachii with three heads.
nodes.includes: Elbow extension and pressing.
nodes.note: Preserved WP 8 id (L3 muscle).

nodes.label: Triceps, long head
nodes.definition: Head crossing the shoulder joint.
nodes.includes: Overhead extensions.
nodes.note: Emphasis claims are qualitative.

nodes.label: Triceps, lateral head
nodes.definition: Outer head.
nodes.includes: Heavy pressing and pushdowns.

nodes.label: Triceps, medial head
nodes.definition: Deep head beneath the other two.
nodes.includes: Elbow extension at all angles.

nodes.label: Anconeus
nodes.definition: Small muscle at the back of the elbow.
nodes.includes: Elbow extension and joint stability.
nodes.note: Rarely a training target.

nodes.label: Forearms
nodes.definition: Muscles between elbow and wrist that move the wrist, fingers and forearm.
nodes.includes: Wrist flexors and extensors, brachioradialis, pronators, supinators.
nodes.note: Preserved WP 8 id (L2 group).

nodes.label: Wrist and finger flexors
nodes.definition: Muscles on the palm side of the forearm.
nodes.includes: Wrist flexion, gripping and holding.

nodes.label: Flexor carpi radialis
nodes.definition: Flexor on the thumb side of the forearm.
nodes.includes: Wrist flexion and radial deviation.

nodes.label: Flexor carpi ulnaris
nodes.definition: Flexor on the little-finger side of the forearm.
nodes.includes: Wrist flexion and ulnar deviation.

nodes.label: Finger flexors
nodes.definition: Flexor digitorum superficialis and profundus.
nodes.includes: Gripping, hanging and carrying.
nodes.note: Cross the wrist; filed under wrist flexors.

nodes.label: Wrist and finger extensors
nodes.definition: Muscles on the back of the forearm.
nodes.includes: Wrist extension and holding the wrist neutral under load.

nodes.label: Extensor carpi radialis
nodes.definition: Longus and brevis, on the thumb side.
nodes.includes: Wrist extension and radial deviation.

nodes.label: Extensor carpi ulnaris
nodes.definition: Extensor on the little-finger side.
nodes.includes: Wrist extension and ulnar deviation.

nodes.label: Finger extensors
nodes.definition: Extensor digitorum and related muscles.
nodes.includes: Opening the hand and finger extension.

nodes.label: Brachioradialis
nodes.definition: Forearm muscle on the thumb side that bends the elbow.
nodes.includes: Elbow flexion with a neutral or pronated forearm (reverse curl, hammer curl).
nodes.note: Debatable: an elbow flexor placed under Forearms as planned.

nodes.label: Forearm pronators
nodes.definition: Pronator teres and pronator quadratus.
nodes.includes: Turning the palm down.

nodes.label: Forearm supinators
nodes.definition: Supinator muscle (the biceps also supinates).
nodes.includes: Turning the palm up.

nodes.label: Trunk
nodes.definition: The abdominal wall and the deep muscles that brace the spine and pelvis.
nodes.includes: Abdominals, obliques and pelvic floor.
nodes.note: Training tranche 5.6 also covers Lower back, whose region is Back.

nodes.label: Abs
nodes.definition: Front abdominal wall muscles.
nodes.includes: Rectus abdominis and transversus abdominis.
nodes.note: Preserved WP 8 id (L2 group).

nodes.label: Rectus abdominis
nodes.definition: Paired vertical muscle at the front of the abdomen.
nodes.includes: Trunk flexion and resisting trunk extension.
nodes.note: Not split into upper and lower parts: a single muscle with segmental activity.

nodes.label: Transversus abdominis
nodes.definition: Deepest abdominal layer wrapping around the trunk.
nodes.includes: Bracing and drawing in the abdominal wall.
nodes.note: Rarely a primary target; tag as secondary for bracing work.

nodes.label: Obliques
nodes.definition: Muscles on the sides of the abdomen.
nodes.includes: External and internal oblique.
nodes.note: Preserved WP 8 id (L2 group).

nodes.label: External oblique
nodes.definition: Outer oblique layer.
nodes.includes: Trunk rotation to the opposite side, side flexion, flexion.

nodes.label: Internal oblique
nodes.definition: Oblique layer under the external oblique.
nodes.includes: Trunk rotation to the same side, side flexion.

nodes.label: Pelvic floor
nodes.definition: Muscles that form the base of the pelvis. Content excluded by owner decision 2026-11-05 (the id is kept).
nodes.includes: Pelvic floor contraction and relaxation exercises.
nodes.note: Content excluded by owner decision 2026-11-05: no pelvic floor exercises are authored. The node and its id are kept in the reference data; it carries no coverage entries.

nodes.label: Hip and pelvis
nodes.definition: The hip joint and the muscles that move the thigh at the hip.
nodes.includes: Glutes, hip abductors, adductors, hip flexors and deep hip rotators.

nodes.label: Glutes
nodes.definition: Muscle group of the gluteus maximus, medius and minimus.
nodes.includes: Hip extension, hip abduction, pelvic stability.
nodes.excludes: Tensor fasciae latae (Abductors) and deep rotators.
nodes.note: Preserved WP 8 id (L2 group).

nodes.label: Gluteus maximus
nodes.definition: Largest gluteal muscle.
nodes.includes: Hip extension and external rotation (thrusts, bridges, hinges, squats).
nodes.note: Upper and lower fibres are not tagged separately.

nodes.label: Gluteus medius
nodes.definition: Fan-shaped muscle on the outer pelvis.
nodes.includes: Hip abduction and single-leg pelvic stability.
nodes.note: Functionally a hip abductor but filed under Glutes: one parent per node.

nodes.label: Gluteus minimus
nodes.definition: Smallest gluteal muscle, under the medius.
nodes.includes: Hip abduction and internal rotation.
nodes.note: Functionally a hip abductor but filed under Glutes: one parent per node.

nodes.label: Abductors
nodes.definition: Muscles that move the thigh out to the side, as filed here.
nodes.includes: Tensor fasciae latae and any exercise tagged as hip abduction at group level.
nodes.excludes: Gluteus medius and minimus (filed under Glutes).
nodes.note: Preserved WP 8 id (L2 group). Known limitation: most abduction work is done by gluteus medius and minimus; tag them as well when the exercise targets them.

nodes.label: Tensor fasciae latae
nodes.definition: Small muscle at the front-outer hip feeding the iliotibial band.
nodes.includes: Hip abduction, flexion and internal rotation.

nodes.label: Adductors
nodes.definition: Muscles on the inner thigh that pull the leg towards the midline.
nodes.includes: Adductor magnus, longus, brevis, gracilis and pectineus.
nodes.note: Preserved WP 8 id (L2 group). Placement under Hip and pelvis is debatable (see anatomy.md section 5, item 16).

nodes.label: Adductor magnus
nodes.definition: Largest adductor with an adductor part and a hamstring part.
nodes.includes: Hip adduction and, through its rear part, hip extension.

nodes.label: Adductor magnus, adductor part
nodes.definition: Front part of adductor magnus.
nodes.includes: Hip adduction.

nodes.label: Adductor magnus, hamstring part
nodes.definition: Rear part of adductor magnus.
nodes.includes: Hip extension in deep squats and hinges.
nodes.note: Tag rarely; use only when the movement clearly loads deep hip extension.

nodes.label: Adductor longus
nodes.definition: Long, thin inner-thigh muscle.
nodes.includes: Hip adduction and flexion.

nodes.label: Adductor brevis
nodes.definition: Short adductor beneath the longus.
nodes.includes: Hip adduction.

nodes.label: Gracilis
nodes.definition: Thin strap muscle on the inner thigh.
nodes.includes: Hip adduction and knee flexion.

nodes.label: Pectineus
nodes.definition: Small muscle at the top of the inner thigh.
nodes.includes: Hip adduction and flexion.

nodes.label: Hip flexors
nodes.definition: Muscles that lift the thigh towards the trunk.
nodes.includes: Iliopsoas and sartorius. Rectus femoris is filed under Quadriceps.
nodes.note: Functional group; rectus femoris stays under Quadriceps (one parent per node).

nodes.label: Iliopsoas
nodes.definition: Psoas major and iliacus together.
nodes.includes: Hip flexion and lumbar stabilisation.

nodes.label: Psoas major
nodes.definition: Muscle from the lumbar spine to the thigh.
nodes.includes: Hip flexion.

nodes.label: Iliacus
nodes.definition: Muscle lining the inside of the pelvis.
nodes.includes: Hip flexion.

nodes.label: Sartorius
nodes.definition: Long strap muscle across the front of the thigh.
nodes.includes: Hip flexion, abduction and external rotation; knee flexion.
nodes.note: Debatable: lies in the anterior thigh but is filed with the hip flexors.

nodes.label: Deep hip rotators
nodes.definition: Small muscles behind the hip joint that turn the thigh outwards: piriformis, obturator internus and externus, the gemelli and quadratus femoris.
nodes.includes: Hip external rotation. Only piriformis has its own node; the obturators, gemelli and quadratus femoris are covered by this group node and are tagged at the group (L2).
nodes.note: Reduced from five L3 nodes to one: the smaller rotators cannot be trained separately.

nodes.label: Piriformis
nodes.definition: Pear-shaped muscle from the sacrum to the thigh bone.
nodes.includes: Hip external rotation.
nodes.note: Only deep rotator with its own node.

nodes.label: Thigh
nodes.definition: The thigh between hip and knee.
nodes.includes: Quadriceps and hamstrings.
nodes.excludes: Adductor group and hip flexors (Hip and pelvis).

nodes.label: Quadriceps
nodes.definition: Four-headed muscle at the front of the thigh.
nodes.includes: Knee extension in squats, presses, lunges and extensions.
nodes.excludes: Hip flexors other than rectus femoris.
nodes.note: Preserved WP 8 id (L2 group).

nodes.label: Rectus femoris
nodes.definition: Quadriceps head that crosses the hip.
nodes.includes: Knee extension and hip flexion.
nodes.note: Functions as a hip flexor but filed under Quadriceps.

nodes.label: Vastus lateralis
nodes.definition: Outer quadriceps head.
nodes.includes: Knee extension.

nodes.label: Vastus medialis
nodes.definition: Inner quadriceps head on the front of the thigh.
nodes.includes: Knee extension through the whole range.
nodes.note: The commonly used 'VMO' label is not modelled separately. The idea that this head works only in the last degrees of extension is a myth and is not used here.

nodes.label: Vastus intermedius
nodes.definition: Deep quadriceps head under rectus femoris.
nodes.includes: Knee extension.

nodes.label: Hamstrings
nodes.definition: Muscle group at the back of the thigh.
nodes.includes: Knee flexion and hip extension.
nodes.note: Preserved WP 8 id (L2 group).

nodes.label: Biceps femoris
nodes.definition: Outer hamstring with two heads.
nodes.includes: Knee flexion and hip extension.

nodes.label: Biceps femoris, long head
nodes.definition: Head crossing hip and knee.
nodes.includes: Hip extension and knee flexion.

nodes.label: Biceps femoris, short head
nodes.definition: Head crossing the knee only.
nodes.includes: Knee flexion, including when the hip is already extended.

nodes.label: Semitendinosus
nodes.definition: Inner hamstring with a long tendon.
nodes.includes: Knee flexion and hip extension.

nodes.label: Semimembranosus
nodes.definition: Deep inner hamstring.
nodes.includes: Knee flexion and hip extension.

nodes.label: Lower leg and ankle
nodes.definition: The lower leg between knee and ankle, including the muscles that move the ankle and foot.
nodes.includes: Calf, shin and lateral lower-leg muscles.

nodes.label: Calves
nodes.definition: Muscles at the back of the lower leg that point the foot down.
nodes.includes: Gastrocnemius and soleus.
nodes.note: Preserved WP 8 id (L2 group).

nodes.label: Gastrocnemius
nodes.definition: Two-headed calf muscle crossing knee and ankle.
nodes.includes: Plantar flexion, strongest with the knee straight.

nodes.label: Gastrocnemius, medial head
nodes.definition: Inner head of the calf muscle.
nodes.includes: Plantar flexion with the knee straight.
nodes.note: Heads are tagged only when an exercise deliberately changes foot position; qualitative.

nodes.label: Gastrocnemius, lateral head
nodes.definition: Outer head of the calf muscle.
nodes.includes: Plantar flexion with the knee straight.

nodes.label: Soleus
nodes.definition: Flat calf muscle under the gastrocnemius.
nodes.includes: Plantar flexion, strongest with the knee bent.

nodes.label: Shin muscles
nodes.definition: Front compartment of the lower leg.
nodes.includes: Tibialis anterior and toe extensors.

nodes.label: Tibialis anterior
nodes.definition: Muscle along the front of the shin.
nodes.includes: Dorsiflexion and foot inversion.
nodes.note: The plan proposed this as an L2 node; here it is L3 under a new L2 compartment so related muscles have a parent.

nodes.label: Toe extensors
nodes.definition: Extensor digitorum longus and extensor hallucis longus.
nodes.includes: Lifting the toes and assisting dorsiflexion.

nodes.label: Outer lower-leg muscles
nodes.definition: Lateral compartment of the lower leg.
nodes.includes: Fibularis (peroneal) muscles.

nodes.label: Fibularis longus
nodes.definition: Outer lower-leg muscle (peroneus longus).
nodes.includes: Foot eversion and ankle stability.

nodes.label: Fibularis brevis
nodes.definition: Shorter outer lower-leg muscle (peroneus brevis).
nodes.includes: Foot eversion.

nodes.label: Deep calf muscles
nodes.definition: Deep back compartment of the lower leg.
nodes.includes: Tibialis posterior and toe flexors.

nodes.label: Tibialis posterior
nodes.definition: Deep muscle supporting the arch.
nodes.includes: Foot inversion and arch support.

nodes.label: Toe flexors
nodes.definition: Flexor digitorum longus and flexor hallucis longus.
nodes.includes: Curling the toes and push-off.

nodes.label: Full body
nodes.definition: Non-anatomical classification for conditioning and whole-body work (flagged non-anatomical).
nodes.includes: Cardio and conditioning exercises with no defensible muscle subset.
nodes.excludes: Any anatomical muscle. The node has no children and is excluded from anatomical roll-ups, coverage and attributed muscle set counts (shown separately, labelled non-anatomical).
nodes.note: Flagged non-anatomical L1 node with no children (ADR-0010, approved 2026-11-05). May only be the single primary target of qualifying whole-body or conditioning exercises; never a secondary and never alongside anatomical primaries. Excluded from anatomical roll-ups, coverage and attributed muscle set counts; shown separately in reports labelled non-anatomical.
